utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, will you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honour. This is the case Number IT-97-25/1-PT, The Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the representatives of the Prosecution introduce themselves, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Bill Smith with Christine Moeller and Diane Boles for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Vladimir Domazet, lead counsel representing the accused Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber good morning to all those present, representatives of the OTP, the Defence counsel, the accused, as well as all the staff of this courtroom, Madam Registrar, the legal counsellor, Mr. Usher, the court reporters, as well as the interpreters working in their booths. As you are aware, we are here to attend a Status Conference, the last Status Conference having been held more than three months ago. And pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, we have to hold a Status Conference every 120 days. And it is within that framework that we are holding this Status Conference. Its aim is to consider a series of matters. Those matters were referred to yesterday during the pre-trial meeting held in the presence of the legal officer who reported to me the substance of the meeting held yesterday. So I should like now to review the points we have on our agenda and that refer to the state of affairs in the proceedings. First of all, I should like to address the accused -- I'm sorry, the Prosecution to see how they stand regarding Rule 66(A)(i) and 66(A)(ii) regarding the disclosure of written statements of witnesses, and the 92 bis statements. Could the Prosecution, please, inform me of the progress made with respect to the disclosure of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In relation to disclosure at this stage, Your Honour, the Prosecution has substantially complied with its obligations. As Your Honour is aware, the Prosecution has supplied the Defence the supporting material back in October 2003. That supporting material contained about 47 witness statements, of which the Prosecution would be largely relying on at this stage as witnesses that would be presented if this matter comes to trial. In addition to that, the Prosecution supplied the Defence the open transcripts of the case of the Prosecutor against Krnojelac which was heard at this Tribunal. And as Your Honour is aware, that case is substantially the same case in terms of the crime base that this accused is facing. The witnesses that we called in that case, again, would largely be the same witnesses that we would call in this case. So until such time that the decision on the amended indictment is handed down, the Prosecution at this stage feels it can't do too much more to refine what would be its witness list and the relationships with the Defence counsel, Mr. Domazet, have been quite good. And we have agreed that after the decision of the amended indictment has been handed down, that we would meet comprehensively together, after he has spoken to the accused, and determine what facts may be agreed, what facts would be in dispute. And therefore, we could refine and add to our witness list based on that. Regarding Rule 68, most of the material -- all of the material that the Prosecution is aware of that would fall under Rule 68 has been supplied to the Defence. And it's been supplied in the form of the supporting material, those 47 witness statements, and in relation to the trial testimony in the case of Prosecutor versus Krnojelac. Now, the Defence has been supplied with the Defence testimony as well, and there is some Rule 68 material amongst all of that. As far as it was raised yesterday by the Defence that at this stage he hasn't got the full names of the witnesses of which we've supplied and the statements to him, and it's agreed that the statements have been supplied under pseudonyms, as pseudonyms were given in the previous case. The Prosecutor would be making application to have those pseudonyms lifted for the limited purpose to supply the identity of the witnesses to the Defence. But obviously, not to the public at large. And the Prosecution has made an undertaking to do that in the next few weeks Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. so that the accused can -- it can assist the accused in preparing his Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the explanations given regarding the disclosure in accordance with Rule 66 and 68. Mr. Domazet, do you share the optimism of the Prosecution regarding disclosure, or do you have any reservations or any difficulties? I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no particular problems to raise. Everything said by my learned friend Mr. Smith stands, and I confirm it. I have indeed received the 47 witness statements. The only problem that we raised yesterday was that I don't have the names of the witnesses, but I will have them in about two weeks' time, so there's no problem there either. So there's really no problems on the part of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, there is a decision that needs to be rendered regarding the indictment, which was the subject of several motions. And perhaps by the end of the week we will be rendering our decision. So you will have the ruling of the Chamber regarding the indictment, which will allow you to make further progress in disclosing documents and material. Regarding the communication to the Defence of the names of witnesses heard in the Krnojelac case under pseudonym, of course that question can be very easily resolved. Of course, the Defence needs to know the identity of those witnesses. I would also like to draw the attention of the parties to the fact that as you know, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence envisage that the parties may agree on certain facts or on points of law. Therefore, I would like to encourage the parties to address those matters which would enable us to gain time. Regarding the Prosecution's standpoint, there would be about 47 witnesses who would be called for the trial. This is an approximate figure, which seems to me a very reasonable number. If we don't encounter any other difficulties, we could envisage the following schedule: I am counting on holding the next Status Conference at the beginning of July, because as you know August is the court recess time. So we can't have a hearing in August. But at the beginning of July, the 7th or the 8th of July, we will hold a Status Conference. And then comes July, August, September, and in the last trimester, that is mid-September, if everything goes well, we can envisage the Pre-Trial Conference so as to enable the very expeditious hearing of this case, unless there are any new difficulties that may crop up. So that would be the schedule planned which we should be able to observe without any difficulty, both by the Prosecution and the Defence. There's also another matter that was raised, and that is that the accused, Mr. Rasevic, would like to have a personal lawyer that he knows, and that is Mr. Prodanovic. As this request was made, the question was left on standby regarding this lawyer. And according to what I have been told, it appears that that lawyer cannot unfortunately for Mr. Rasevic assist him as there was a decision taken with regard to him in the meantime. Due to that, Mr. Domazet, you are the designated counsel for the accused. So it appears that this matter of Defence counsel has been resolved by a decision made a few hours ago. I have another point to address on the agenda; that is, the health and conditions of detention for Mr. Rasevic. So can you stand, please, Mr. Rasevic, and tell me in your own language whether you have any particular health problems.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no health problems whatsoever. And as regards the Detention Unit and the behaviour of detention personnel and the other detainees, everything is absolutely in order. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you have no remarks to make regarding your health or conditions of detention. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have nothing to say. Everything is absolutely fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have raised the various items of our agenda. Has the Defence any other matters or points to make which we could discuss at this stage? Mr. Domazet, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the Prosecution, do you have any questions to raise that were not included in the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Nothing further. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The expeditiousness of this hearing testifies to the fact the proceedings are on a good path. I have referred to a decision that will be made shortly regarding the indictment. And as I indicated, we will have a Status Conference at the beginning of July, and I hope that the Prosecution will be in a position to prepare the proper conditions for the Pre-Trial Conference and the trial itself. So I cannot tell you exactly the date for the beginning of trial because as you know, this Tribunal works in three courtrooms which are more or less all busy by the current trials. There's some trials that are on standby, and they will be added to the schedule in due course. And that is the information I'm able to give you today. Thank you. And I invite you to come back at the beginning of July. In the meantime, the legal officer of this Chamber will, in accordance with the rules of procedure, have a meeting with you. Should there be any difficulties, please do not hesitate to inform me about them. Thank you.
